decisions.title: The Wolfsberg questionnaire is not mandatory; a fallback question set is asked in Hazel onboarding
decisions.statement: A bank that does not hold a Wolfsberg questionnaire is not blocked. It answers an equivalent set of questions inside the Hazel onboarding flow instead, and that data is pushed to CoverBase. The questions are asked by the Hazel-built onboarding rather than by CoverBase directly. A bank that does hold a Wolfsberg document continues on the existing path.

evidence.excerpt: Yeah, I think that would be our best approach. Now, I can incorporate some of those questions into Cover Base, but I believe it's better if they come from the Hazel onboarding that the team is working on.
Right. Yeah. If they have a Wolfsberg, keep going. If they don't have a Wolfsberg, answer these questions.
I think Shawn is mentioning that — we will ask them, do you have that? And if not, then we'll ask those questions.

decisions.confidence_note: The conditional path is stated flatly by Joel Olivares, restated by Shantanu Wadodkar and confirmed ("Perfect"). How the fallback is presented is not settled — Joel said "I don't know if that's my decision" about making it dynamic (CAND-Q-001). The question set does not exist yet.

decisions.title: Signing the NDA in Hazel onboarding satisfies the Vanta trust-center NDA requirement
decisions.statement: The applicant bank signs one NDA, in the Hazel onboarding flow. That signature satisfies the NDA that Vanta requires before Hazel's due diligence package is released through the Trust Center, so the bank is not asked to execute a second NDA there.

evidence.excerpt: He's saying that if you sign the NDA through the Hazel onboarding or intake, then the NDA for Vanta would be automatic.
So then the NDA that we do with the member banks is the one that we need to upload, and we're good over there. Okay, so I think I'm good over there.

decisions.confidence_note: Shawn is not on the call; Joel Olivares reads his chat answer aloud and endorses it, and Prashant Sarode accepts it as resolving his objection. Only a first name is given. It states the intended outcome — nobody said who builds the Vanta hand-off or whether Vanta supports it today.

decisions.title: Onboarding does not offer entry of an existing account number
decisions.statement: The onboarding flow does not ask an applicant whether it already holds an account, and does not accept an existing account number. A bank going through intake has no account with Hazel by definition — Participate does not issue accounts, it debits and credits accounts already established under a Hazel member bank — so the option has no case to serve.

evidence.excerpt: There's no such thing as a Participate account. Participate is only going to debit or credit the member banks' accounts that are already established.
So we do not give them the option to enter an account number, because they don't have an account number to enter to begin with, or they wouldn't be following those steps of onboarding.
It was just an initial "should we do that," and now, with your help, we decided no. So she's going to continue the way she had it, Pallavi.

decisions.confidence_note: Joel proposed this earlier in the same call, then withdrew it — on its own not a decision. Promoted under the named-authority exception: he is chairing, rules it out with a reason, says "we decided no", and Diana Plata confirms. The outcome is the status quo, so it changes no code.

decisions.title: CoverBase risk scoring is internal-only; the member portal shows a general status
decisions.statement: The member bank portal never surfaces the CoverBase risk assessment score, risk band or findings. Applicants see only a general application status. The internal Hazel operator opens the CoverBase assessment section to see the score, band and findings, and returns to the HOP portal to request missing information from the bank.

evidence.excerpt: From this point forward, the member bank only sees the appropriate general status. They will never get to know about the internal Cover Base scoring in the member portal.

the internal Hazel operator can open the Cover assessment section and they will get the internal-only review where they will get the risk assessment score, risk band, findings, and related details. And if they find some information is missing, they'll come back to the HOP portal and ask the member bank to provide whatever information is required.

decisions.confidence_note: Presented by Pallavi Bichpuriya as behaviour already built, not deliberated here. Nobody objected and Joel Olivares told her to continue as she had it. Promoted because it is a hard disclosure rule; the librarian should decide whether the deciding record belongs to an earlier session.

decisions.title: Applicant progress is saved for return, and risk questions stay locked until due diligence completes
decisions.statement: The application preserves the bank's progress so a user can save and return to the form at any time. The risk questions are not reachable until the due diligence section is complete.

evidence.excerpt: Hazel will preserve the bank's progress locally so the user can save and return to the form whenever they want. The risk questions remain locked until the due diligence part is completed.

decisions.confidence_note: Demonstrated as built rather than decided. No objection was raised and no owner is named. "Locally" is not defined in the source — whether progress is held client-side or server-side is not stated, and that difference matters for a spec.

decisions.title: The bank confirms, corrects or declines CoverBase-prepared answers, with the source document shown
decisions.statement: Risk answers prepared by CoverBase are returned to the member bank for review. For each one the bank may confirm it, correct it, or state "I'm unable to confirm". The portal tells the bank which already-supplied document each prepared answer was drawn from.

evidence.excerpt: the bank will review, correct, or certify the prepared answers that are returned by Cover Base. Here we will be suggesting: okay, we are taking this information from the documents that you have already provided.
The member bank can confirm, or if they are not able to provide the answer, they will say "I'm unable to confirm," or they can correct their answers.

decisions.confidence_note: Presented as built in the same walkthrough, unopposed but not deliberated. What happens downstream when a bank answers "I'm unable to confirm" — whether it blocks submission or routes to review — is not stated anywhere in the source.

final_takeaways: Nothing in this delta is authoritative. Every item is a candidate for librarian review.
6 candidate decisions, 5 open questions, 4 action items, 4 items deliberately not promoted.
The decision registry is empty, so no candidate could cite a supersedes_id.
Only one topic was genuinely deliberated: what happens when a bank has no Wolfsberg questionnaire. That produced CAND-DEC-001 and CAND-Q-001.
Four candidates are low confidence: CAND-DEC-003 (a withdrawn proposal closed by the chair) and CAND-DEC-004, -005, -006 (behaviour demonstrated as built, unopposed but never deliberated).
CAND-Q-004 reopens whether intake documents live in Databricks, which the 2026-07-16 kickoff appeared to settle.
blocking_reasons: All candidates require librarian approval before any record or ticket can be created.
CAND-DEC-001 cannot be built until the Wolfsberg fallback question set exists (ACT-003) and its presentation is chosen (CAND-Q-001).
The decision registry is empty, so a candidate that restates or narrows an earlier session's call has nothing to cite.
